purpose: Test whether fixed-budget selection of the dominant conditioning-memory tokens improves the four difficult automatic Lean videos, using the author's attention-usage ranking and a matched-budget spatial control.
rationale: A verified read-only replay found that the original dense conditioning memory receives mean 68.8–87.9% of final-layer attention in these videos; the latest full memory receives 0.5–2.0% at its pruning-decision read. Attention mass is descriptive, not a causal importance measure. The original prompt on seq20 and seq23 was made on a labeled-empty frame.
intervention: Leave the first read from the original 4096 conditioning tokens unchanged. Thereafter retain a fixed 1024 conditioning tokens without modifying the stored memory: usage selects the author's top-1024 final-layer attention usages from that first read; the matched generic control selects a fixed 2x2 spatial grid of 1024 tokens. Apply identical indices and ordering to keys, values and positional embeddings through the author's memory materialization, retaining indexed RoPE and the original nonconditioning 25% selection, pointer tokens, initialization, TARR/TCIM and model weights. The operation is a fixed compression step, not confidence gating, a threshold, or re-detection.
validation: Two independent label-free full-retention seq3 no-op replays must exactly match the original indexed video masks and token/position/memory receipts. Two independent label-free seq3 replays each for usage and uniform 1024-token conditions must reproduce selected indices, outputs and traces, preserve exact key/value/position alignment and pointers, and leave model weights and stored conditioning tensors unchanged. No candidate videos until an independent verifier passes all six replays and unit tests.
analysis: Run all four selected videos in both 1024-token conditions, and independently rescore saved masks against the same indexed reference and annotations on all frames and historical matched frames. Include present Dice, empty-frame false alarms, per-sequence differences and runtime/token counts. No labels used in inference and no per-sequence method switching. Four pre-inspected videos are an exploratory diagnostic, not evidence of generalization.
limitations: Pruning the protected prompt memory changes both information and attention normalization; usage versus uniform isolates the importance of the chosen selection only at the same reduced token budget, not the total effect of pruning. First-read usage is derived from the current automatic prompt and may emphasize an incorrect initial object.
